title: Lage utrop med for og så — exclamations
goal: Choose noun-focused for or degree-focused så without question inversion.

objectives.statement: Choose noun-focused for or degree-focused så without question inversion.

spans.value: Maja and Elias have rented a cabin by a fjord. They arrive late in the afternoon and walk through the rooms for the first time.
Ja, og så stille det er her!

blocks.translation: Yes, and how quiet it is here!

spans.value: Se på fjorden. For en utsikt!

blocks.translation: Look at the fjord. What a view!

spans.value: Så blå himmelen er i dag!

blocks.translation: How blue the sky is today!

spans.value: Og for noen store vinduer huset har!

blocks.translation: And what large windows the house has!

spans.value: Ja, så lyst det er inne!

blocks.translation: Yes, how bright it is inside!

The subject comes before the verb. Although the sentence expresses surprise or admiration, it is not a question.

The focus falls on the strength or degree of the description: the apartment is remarkably nice, the kitchen remarkably large, and the runner remarkably fast.

sections.title: The contrast at the heart of the lesson

spans.value: This is the contrast at the heart of the lesson:
sentence packages the reaction around a noun:
sentence highlights the quality or manner:
can make Norwegian learners expect question-like word order. Norwegian
exclamations do not use question inversion.
A normal statement has the subject before the verb:
The corresponding exclamation keeps the subject before the verb:
Do not move the verb in front of the subject:
With that word order and question intonation, the sentence is interpreted as a question rather than the intended exclamation.

statement.value: exclamation, place the description first, then keep the subject before the verb.

spans.value: This also applies when the subject is a pronoun:

blocks.translation: What a peaceful evening we had!

spans.value: Ja, og så klart vi kunne se stjernene!

blocks.translation: Yes, and how clearly we could see the stars!

spans.value: Fint! Dere hadde vel ikke problemer med peisen?

blocks.translation: Good! You didn’t have any problems with the fireplace, did you?

spans.value: Nei. Så lett den var å bruke!

blocks.translation: No. How easy it was to use!

spans.value: Og for en god frokost vi spiste på terrassen!

Imagine that Amir and Nora have arrived at a friend’s birthday party. They react to the decorated room, the large cake, the quiet music, a friend who sings beautifully, and guests who dance energetically.

prompt.value: Complete each cabin reaction. Choose the marker that makes each reaction noun-focused, with the reaction organized around a person, place, or thing.

explanation.value: Use «for en/et/noen» when the noun phrase is the focus. Use «så + adjective/adverb» for degree, and keep subject-before-verb statement order in a full exclamation.

prompt.value: Complete two reactions to the same evening. Focus on the named evening first, then on the degree of its quality. Choose the marker that matches each focus.

spans.value: en vakker kveld! Same evening — degree focus:

prompt.value: Complete two new turns in Ingrid’s cabin conversation. Maja admires a named view; Elias emphasizes the degree of its beauty. Select the complete Norwegian exclamation with the intended marker and statement word order.

For en vakker utsikt vi hadde!

spans.value: Degree focus — how happy the guests are:

prompt.value: Choose an everyday scene at a workplace, shop, or bus stop. Write exactly two Norwegian exclamations about it: one noun-focused reaction about a person or thing using for, and one degree-focused reaction using så. In any full clause, keep the subject before the verb; do not use question inversion.

payload.judge_prompt: Check the response against the task and report evidence for each criterion. Treat any question inversion as failing the word-order criterion.

criteria.instruction: Uses one noun-focused exclamation with for for a person or thing.
Uses one degree-focused exclamation with så.
Keeps the subject before the verb in any full clause and does not use question inversion.
